title: What happens when the AI bubble pops?
excerpt: From the bicycle frenzy to the dot-com boom to today’s AI race, financial history is littered with bubbles. So what happens when they pop?
content_html:
Five experts weigh in.

The mania had started with something real. The safety bicycle: equal wheels, pneumatic tires, a chain drive. The first bicycle model where the rider’s feet could actually touch the road if they needed to stop.

Too bad speculators didn’t keep their feet on solid ground.

“Suddenly, everyone wants to own a bicycle,” says Will Quinn, associate professor of finance at Queen’s University Belfast and co-author of Boom and Bust: A Global History of Financial Bubbles.

The year was 1897 and the bicycle boom had hit Birmingham hard. Tradesmen north of the city bent and brazed steel into frames. When the owner of Dunlop Tires, Ernest Terah Hooley, saw the surge, he jumped. He bribed journalists, packed company boards with noblemen and bought companies for cheap and sold them to the public at a markup.


Ernest Hooley, one of the British entrepreneurs behind the Birmingham bicycle boom. He’d go on to declare bankruptcy four times. (Photo by the Print Collector/Getty Images)

People began daytrading bicycle shares. Nearly every small bicycle company in Birmingham, ~400, went public; there was a rush on the London Stock Exchange and share prices boomed by 10x.

“About a year after that, three quarters of them have gone bankrupt,” says Quinn, who has studied 300 years of financial bubbles.

At the time, The Economist wrote that investors had subscribed millions “on the assumption that high prices would be maintained, but that delusion has been rudely knocked on the head."

By the end of 1898, the small investors who had bought in late lost the most; the promoters and early insiders had long since cashed out.

But it wasn’t all bad: it created jobs. It left thousands with bicycles. And it laid the foundation for what would become the automotive industry.


The bicycle boom in Birmingham inspired new bike-friendly women’s clothing designs too. (Photo by London Stereoscopic Company/Hulton Archive/Getty Images)

From the bicycle frenzy to the dot-com boom to today’s AI race, financial history is littered with bubbles.

So what happens when they pop?

For Quinn and his co-author, Queen’s University Belfast professor John Turner, the bubble is a poor metaphor. They prefer fire.

The necessary ingredients for this kind of fire, according to Turner:

  • Fuel: from low interest rates and freely available credit.
  • Marketability: regulatory or technological changes that enable people to buy and sell the bubble asset more easily.
  • Speculators: new investors entering the market, and experienced investors unable to short the market.

From there, Turner says, you need a spark: a radical new technology, let’s say, that promises to upend the world.

With the caveat that no one can predict the future (or, as Georgetown University finance professor Jim Angel told The Hustle, “you really only know after the fact, and everybody wakes up with a hangover and goes, ‘what were we thinking?’”), we asked five experts to weigh in on what an AI bubble would mean for the stock market, the job market, and the everyday lives of Americans.

For the stock market

First off, the amount of money being spent on AI is unprecedented. Morgan Stanley predicted hyperscalers will spend a collective $1.4T by 2028. Wells Fargo estimated $1.1T by 2027.

“It’s an extraordinary amount of money,” says Ryan Cummings, chief of staff at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policymaking.

That kind of spend brings behemoth revenue expectations for the companies on the receiving end of the outlay, like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Alphabet.

“If you don’t hit those revenues this year, you need more next year,” he says. “The burden increases over time the longer you go on without hitting those targets.”


Investors are watching how capital expenditure spending on the AI infrastructure build-out tracks against revenue. (Photo by Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

And there’s good reason to be wary of much-touted upcoming IPOs from Anthropic and OpenAI.

“All these firms are receiving these very, very high valuations,” Cummings says. “But they’re all being priced as though they’re all going to be the winner of AI. We know not all firms are going to make it.”

Still, if the bubble does pop, most of the damage will be localized to investors unless major institutions are borrowing money to try to capitalize on the boom.

“You don’t know who’s swimming naked til the tide goes out,” Angel says. “To discover some banks lost their shirts — that can have knock-on effects through the rest of the economy.”

For the job market

Like everything else AI-related, experts are divided on what it will mean for the job market.

“In the short term, there’s a construction boom,” says Azeem Azhar, tech entrepreneur and founder of Exponential Views research group. “From a labor market perspective, that’s a really, really good thing because it creates all sorts of new jobs.”


Azeem Azhar speaks at a conference on “If this is an AI bubble, what comes next?” in November 2025. (Photo by Jordan Peck/Getty Images for Business of Fashion)

Data center infrastructure means construction jobs — one 2025 report funded by Meta estimated 4.7m.

But those jobs are temporary. And data centers themselves require just 50 to 200 people to run them. In the meantime, according to data from Goldman Sachs, AI substitution wiped out roughly 25k jobs per month in the past year, while augmentation added back about 9k.

“The theory that AI will suppress office jobs because it can summarize emails seems to hold up,” he says.

Still, Azhar says, it’s too soon to tell what kinds of jobs AI will create. When the internet was invented, he says, it spawned complementary businesses now worth billions. He predicts AI will cause the same creative surge.

For your retirement fund

If you’re a young person stressing about the AI bubble’s impact on your retirement fund, Cummings has a piece of advice.

“Just look at a picture of the S&P 500,” he says. “I’m just leaving my money in the market.”

More broadly, though, bubbles can trigger something called the wealth effect.

Let’s say you need $2m for retirement, and your 401k shows that you have $2.5m. There’s froth to spend on a nice car or a home renovation. Suddenly, the stock market goes down and your nest egg looks more like $1.5m.

“You’re cancelling that vacation, not getting the new car, not buying the new appliance,” Cummings says. “That puts a decline on the entire economy.”

That possibility is something Cummings is watching warily. “I would be very surprised if we got through 2028 without a recession,” he says.


Amazon builds out a massive data center in rural Virginia. (Photo by Jim West/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

That could leave GenX facing a retirement crisis. Just 14% of them have a traditional pension, compared to 56% of boomers, according to a report from Alliance’s Retirement Income Institute, making them more reliant on the aftershocks of a stock market bubble.

It took the S&P 500 years to come back from the dot-com bust in 2002: Around five years to get back to its high point, before the 2008 financial crisis wiped it out again. It wasn’t until 2013 that it fully recovered.

Another difference in this bubble, Turner says, is how much the everyday investor might not realize their exposure. In previous bubbles, you could choose whether to invest in the bubble stocks or not. Today, ~$23T is invested in ETFs, which weren’t nearly as prominent back in the dot-com boom.

“If you’ve got an S&P 500 tracker fund, 35% of that tracker is in those big Magnificent Seven stocks, being driven by the AI boom,” he says. “They’re going to be exposed to this in a way that maybe they hadn’t been in previous bubbles.”

For your everyday life

The word bubble gets tossed around a lot. But there’s a critical difference between a potential AI bubble and, say, the housing bubble of 2008.

Like the dot-com bubble before it, the AI bubble is, so far, largely fueled by equity. The housing bubble was propped up by debt, which made its consequences farther reaching.

“There’s an expectation that bubbles are always really bad,” Quinn says. “It’s not a given that the bursting of the bubble will be economically devastating, not at all.”

Whether AI radically changes the world or not, for Cummings, the solution remains the same.

“It’s having a more robust social safety net,” he says. “It’s the same lesson to the dot-com boom, to the financial crisis, to Covid. You find people who lost their job and give them support. They have a roof over their head, food in their bellies, care if they have some sort of medical condition. People talk in lots of complicated ways about what the lesson is. It’s not that complicated.”


The Nasdaq fell 77% after the dot-com bubble burst. (Photo by Spencer Platt/Getty Images)

Turner returns to his fire metaphor. Fires can have devastating consequences. When the dot-com bubble burst, nearly 5k companies went under and the Nasdaq fell 77%. The year the housing bubble burst, 860k American properties were repossessed.

Still, he says, technology bubbles tend to leave less damage, in part an overvaluation and subsequent crash still leaves behind a real, tangible product we can use.

“Fire can be good for some ecosystems,” he says. “Fire revitalizes. That’s true with a lot of technological bubbles, they actually help revitalize the ecosystem.”

Consider the dot-com boom and bust. It minted millionaires and led to a recession, he says.

“It also gave us the internet. We got this amazing information communications technology infrastructure build-out,” he says. “And, you know, society benefitted from it.”

sentences.en: By the end of 1898, the small investors who had bought in late lost the most; the promoters and early insiders had long since cashed out.
sentences.zh: 到1898年底，迟到的小投资者损失最大；发起人和早期内部人士早已套现。

sentences.en: But it wasn’t all bad: it created jobs.
sentences.zh: 但这也不全是坏事：它创造了就业机会。

sentences.en: It left thousands with bicycles.
sentences.zh: 数千人留下了自行车。

sentences.en: And it laid the foundation for what would become the automotive industry.
sentences.zh: 它为后来的汽车工业奠定了基础。

sentences.en: The bicycle boom in Birmingham inspired new bike-friendly women’s clothing designs too.
sentences.zh: 伯明翰的自行车热潮也激发了新的适合自行车的女装设计。

sentences.en: (Photo by London Stereoscopic Company/Hulton Archive/Getty Images) From the bicycle frenzy to the dot-com boom to today’s AI race, financial history is littered with bubbles.
sentences.zh: （伦敦立体公司/Hulton Archive/Getty Images 拍摄）从自行车热潮到互联网泡沫，再到今天的人工智能竞赛，金融史上充满了泡沫。

sentences.en: So what happens when they pop?
sentences.zh: 那么当它们弹出时会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: For Quinn and his co-author, Queen’s University Belfast professor John Turner, the bubble is a poor metaphor.
sentences.zh: 对于奎因和他的合著者、贝尔法斯特女王大学教授约翰·特纳来说，泡沫是一个糟糕的比喻。

sentences.en: They prefer fire.
sentences.zh: 他们更喜欢火。

sentences.en: The necessary ingredients for this kind of fire, according to Turner: Fuel: from low interest rates and freely available credit.
sentences.zh: 特纳认为，引发这种火灾的必要因素是： 燃料：低利率和免费信贷。

sentences.en: Marketability: regulatory or technological changes that enable people to buy and sell the bubble asset more easily.
sentences.zh: 适销性：监管或技术的变化使人们能够更轻松地买卖泡沫资产。

sentences.en: Speculators: new investors entering the market, and experienced investors unable to short the market.
sentences.zh: 投机者：新进入市场的投资者，以及无法做空市场的经验丰富的投资者。

sentences.en: From there, Turner says, you need a spark: a radical new technology, let’s say, that promises to upend the world.
sentences.zh: 特纳说，从那时起，你需要一个火花：一种激进的新技术，比方说，它有望颠覆世界。

sentences.en: With the caveat that no one can predict the future (or, as Georgetown University finance professor Jim Angel told The Hustle, “you really only know after the fact, and everybody wakes up with a hangover and goes, ‘what were we thinking?’”), we asked five experts to weigh in on what an AI bubble would mean for the stock market, the job market, and the everyday lives of Americans.
sentences.zh: 需要注意的是，没有人可以预测未来（或者，正如乔治城大学金融学教授 Jim Angel 告诉 The Hustle 的那样，“你真的只能在事后才知道，每个人都在宿醉中醒来，然后问‘我们在想什么？’”），我们请了五位专家来权衡人工智能泡沫对股市、就业市场和美国人的日常生活意味着什么。

sentences.en: For the stock market First off, the amount of money being spent on AI is unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 对于股票市场 首先，在人工智能上花费的资金是前所未有的。

sentences.en: Morgan Stanley predicted hyperscalers will spend a collective $1.4T by 2028.
sentences.zh: 摩根士丹利 (Morgan Stanley) 预测，到 2028 年，超大规模企业的总支出将达到 1.4 吨。

sentences.en: Wells Fargo estimated $1.1T by 2027.
sentences.zh: 富国银行估计到 2027 年将达到 1.1 吨。

sentences.en: “It’s an extraordinary amount of money,” says Ryan Cummings, chief of staff at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policymaking.
sentences.zh: “这是一笔非凡的资金，”斯坦福经济政策制定研究所幕僚长瑞安·卡明斯 (Ryan Cummings) 表示。

sentences.en: That kind of spend brings behemoth revenue expectations for the companies on the receiving end of the outlay, like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Alphabet.
sentences.zh: 这种支出为 Anthropic、OpenAI 和 Alphabet 等接受支出的公司带来了巨大的收入预期。

sentences.en: “If you don’t hit those revenues this year, you need more next year,” he says.
sentences.zh: “如果你今年没有达到这些收入，明年你就需要更多，”他说。

sentences.en: “The burden increases over time the longer you go on without hitting those targets.”
sentences.zh: “随着时间的推移，如果你没有达到这些目标，负担就会增加。”

sentences.en: Investors are watching how capital expenditure spending on the AI infrastructure build-out tracks against revenue.
sentences.zh: 投资者正在关注人工智能基础设施建设的资本支出与收入的关系。

sentences.en: (Photo by Michael M.
sentences.zh: （摄影：迈克尔·M.

sentences.en: Santiago/Getty Images) And there’s good reason to be wary of much-touted upcoming IPOs from Anthropic and OpenAI.
sentences.zh: 圣地亚哥/盖蒂图片社）并且有充分的理由对 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 即将进行的 IPO 保持警惕。

sentences.en: “All these firms are receiving these very, very high valuations,” Cummings says.
sentences.zh: “所有这些公司都获得了非常非常高的估值，”卡明斯说。

sentences.en: “But they’re all being priced as though they’re all going to be the winner of AI.
sentences.zh: “但它们的定价就好像它们都将成为人工智能的赢家一样。

sentences.en: We know not all firms are going to make it.”
sentences.zh: 我们知道并非所有公司都能成功。”

sentences.en: Still, if the bubble does pop, most of the damage will be localized to investors unless major institutions are borrowing money to try to capitalize on the boom.
sentences.zh: 不过，如果泡沫确实破裂，大部分损失将集中在投资者身上，除非主要机构借钱试图利用繁荣。

sentences.en: “You don’t know who’s swimming naked til the tide goes out,” Angel says.
sentences.zh: “直到潮水退去，你都不知道谁在裸泳，”安吉尔说。

sentences.en: “To discover some banks lost their shirts — that can have knock-on effects through the rest of the economy.”
sentences.zh: “发现一些银行血本无归——这可能会对其他经济领域产生连锁反应。”

sentences.en: For the job market Like everything else AI-related, experts are divided on what it will mean for the job market.
sentences.zh: 对于就业市场 就像其他与人工智能相关的事情一样，专家们对于人工智能对就业市场意味着什么也存在分歧。

sentences.en: “In the short term, there’s a construction boom,” says Azeem Azhar, tech entrepreneur and founder of Exponential Views research group.
sentences.zh: “短期内会出现建筑热潮，”科技企业家兼指数观点研究小组创始人阿齐姆·阿扎尔 (Azeem Azhar) 表示。

sentences.en: “From a labor market perspective, that’s a really, really good thing because it creates all sorts of new jobs.”
sentences.zh: “从劳动力市场的角度来看，这是一件非常非常好的事情，因为它创造了各种各样的新就业机会。”

sentences.en: Azeem Azhar speaks at a conference on “If this is an AI bubble, what comes next?”
sentences.zh: 阿兹姆·阿扎尔 (Azeem Azhar) 在一场题为“如果这是人工智能泡沫，接下来会发生什么？”的会议上发表讲话

sentences.en: in November 2025.
(Photo by Jordan Peck/Getty Images for Business of Fashion) Data center infrastructure means construction jobs — one 2025 report funded by Meta estimated 4.7m.
sentences.zh: （摄影：Jordan Peck/Getty Images for Business of Fashion）数据中心基础设施意味着建筑工作——Meta 资助的一份 2025 年报告估计有 470 万个工作岗位。

sentences.en: But those jobs are temporary.
sentences.zh: 但这些工作都是暂时的。

sentences.en: And data centers themselves require just 50 to 200 people to run them.
sentences.zh: 数据中心本身只需要 50 到 200 人来运行。

sentences.en: In the meantime, according to data from Goldman Sachs, AI substitution wiped out roughly 25k jobs per month in the past year, while augmentation added back about 9k.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，根据高盛的数据，过去一年中，人工智能替代每月大约消除 2.5 万个工作岗位，而增强技术则增加了约 9,000 个工作岗位。

sentences.en: “The theory that AI will suppress office jobs because it can summarize emails seems to hold up,” he says.
sentences.zh: “人工智能会因为可以总结电子邮件而抑制办公室工作的理论似乎站得住脚，”他说。

sentences.en: Still, Azhar says, it’s too soon to tell what kinds of jobs AI will create.
sentences.zh: 不过，阿扎尔表示，现在判断人工智能将创造什么样的就业机会还为时过早。

sentences.en: When the internet was invented, he says, it spawned complementary businesses now worth billions.
sentences.zh: 他说，当互联网发明时，它催生了现在价值数十亿美元的互补业务。

sentences.en: He predicts AI will cause the same creative surge.
sentences.zh: 他预测人工智能将引发同样的创造力激增。

sentences.en: For your retirement fund If you’re a young person stressing about the AI bubble’s impact on your retirement fund, Cummings has a piece of advice.
sentences.zh: 对于你的退休基金如果你是一个年轻人，担心人工智能泡沫对你的退休基金的影响，卡明斯有一条建议。

sentences.en: “Just look at a picture of the S&P 500,” he says.
sentences.zh: “看看标准普尔 500 指数的图片就知道了，”他说。

sentences.en: “I’m just leaving my money in the market.”
sentences.zh: “我只是把钱留在市场上。”

sentences.en: More broadly, though, bubbles can trigger something called the wealth effect.
sentences.zh: 但更广泛地说，泡沫可能引发财富效应。

sentences.en: Let’s say you need $2m for retirement, and your 401k shows that you have $2.5m.
sentences.zh: 假设您需要 200 万美元用于退休，而您的 401k 显示您有 250 万美元。

sentences.en: There’s froth to spend on a nice car or a home renovation.
sentences.zh: 有钱可以花在买一辆漂亮的汽车或装修房屋上。

sentences.en: Suddenly, the stock market goes down and your nest egg looks more like $1.5m.
sentences.zh: 突然，股市下跌，你的存款看起来只剩下 150 万美元了。

sentences.en: “You’re cancelling that vacation, not getting the new car, not buying the new appliance,” Cummings says.
sentences.zh: 卡明斯说：“你会取消假期，不会得到新车，也不会购买新电器。”

sentences.en: “That puts a decline on the entire economy.”
sentences.zh: “这会导致整个经济下滑。”

sentences.en: That possibility is something Cummings is watching warily.
sentences.zh: 卡明斯正在警惕地关注这种可能性。

sentences.en: “I would be very surprised if we got through 2028 without a recession,” he says.
sentences.zh: 他表示：“如果 2028 年我们没有出现衰退，我会感到非常惊讶。”

sentences.en: Amazon builds out a massive data center in rural Virginia.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊在弗吉尼亚州农村地区建立了一个大型数据中心。

sentences.en: (Photo by Jim West/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images) That could leave GenX facing a retirement crisis.
sentences.zh: （吉姆·韦斯特/UCG/Universal Images Group 通过 Getty Images 拍摄）这可能会让 GenX 面临退休危机。

sentences.en: Just 14% of them have a traditional pension, compared to 56% of boomers, according to a report from Alliance’s Retirement Income Institute, making them more reliant on the aftershocks of a stock market bubble.
sentences.zh: 根据联盟退休收入研究所的一份报告，只有 14% 的人拥有传统养老金，而婴儿潮一代的这一比例为 56%，这使得他们更加依赖股市泡沫的余震。

sentences.en: It took the S&P 500 years to come back from the dot-com bust in 2002: Around five years to get back to its high point, before the 2008 financial crisis wiped it out again.
sentences.zh: 标准普尔 500 指数花了 500 年才从 2002 年的互联网泡沫破灭中恢复过来：大约用了五年时间才回到高点，然后 2008 年金融危机再次将其摧毁。

sentences.en: It wasn’t until 2013 that it fully recovered.
sentences.zh: 直到2013年才完全恢复。

sentences.en: Another difference in this bubble, Turner says, is how much the everyday investor might not realize their exposure.
sentences.zh: 特纳说，这个泡沫的另一个区别是，普通投资者可能没有意识到自己的风险敞口有多少。

sentences.en: In previous bubbles, you could choose whether to invest in the bubble stocks or not.
sentences.zh: 在以前的泡沫中，你可以选择是否投资泡沫股票。

sentences.en: Today, ~$23T is invested in ETFs, which weren’t nearly as prominent back in the dot-com boom.
sentences.zh: 如今，约有 23T 美元投资于 ETF，而在互联网繁荣时期，ETF 并没有那么突出。

sentences.en: “If you’ve got an S&P 500 tracker fund, 35% of that tracker is in those big Magnificent Seven stocks, being driven by the AI boom,” he says.
sentences.zh: 他表示：“如果你有一只标准普尔 500 指数追踪基金，那么该追踪基金的 35% 都投资于受人工智能热潮推动的七大股票。”

sentences.en: “They’re going to be exposed to this in a way that maybe they hadn’t been in previous bubbles.”
sentences.zh: “他们将以一种在以前的泡沫中可能没有经历过的方式接触到这种情况。”

sentences.en: For your everyday life The word bubble gets tossed around a lot.
sentences.zh: 对于您的日常生活 泡沫这个词经常被提及。

sentences.en: But there’s a critical difference between a potential AI bubble and, say, the housing bubble of 2008.
sentences.zh: 但潜在的人工智能泡沫与 2008 年的房地产泡沫之间存在着重大区别。

sentences.en: Like the dot-com bubble before it, the AI bubble is, so far, largely fueled by equity.
sentences.zh: 与之前的互联网泡沫一样，迄今为止，人工智能泡沫主要是由股权推动的。

sentences.en: The housing bubble was propped up by debt, which made its consequences farther reaching.
sentences.zh: 房地产泡沫是由债务支撑的，这使其后果更加深远。

sentences.en: “There’s an expectation that bubbles are always really bad,” Quinn says.
sentences.zh: “人们普遍认为泡沫总是很糟糕，”奎因说。

sentences.en: “It’s not a given that the bursting of the bubble will be economically devastating, not at all.”
sentences.zh: “泡沫的破裂不会对经济造成毁灭性的影响，一点也不。”

sentences.en: Whether AI radically changes the world or not, for Cummings, the solution remains the same.
sentences.zh: 无论人工智能是否从根本上改变世界，对于卡明斯来说，解决方案都是一样的。

sentences.en: “It’s having a more robust social safety net,” he says.
sentences.zh: “它拥有更强大的社会安全网，”他说。

sentences.en: “It’s the same lesson to the dot-com boom, to the financial crisis, to Covid.
sentences.zh: “对于互联网繁荣、金融危机和新冠疫情来说，这都是同样的教训。

sentences.en: You find people who lost their job and give them support.
sentences.zh: 您找到失业的人并为他们提供支持。

sentences.en: They have a roof over their head, food in their bellies, care if they have some sort of medical condition.
sentences.zh: 他们头上有屋顶，肚子里有食物，如果他们有某种健康状况，他们会得到照顾。

sentences.en: People talk in lots of complicated ways about what the lesson is.
sentences.zh: 人们用很多复杂的方式谈论教训是什么。

sentences.en: It’s not that complicated.”
sentences.zh: 事情没那么复杂。”

sentences.en: The Nasdaq fell 77% after the dot-com bubble burst.
sentences.zh: 互联网泡沫破裂后，纳斯达克指数下跌了 77%。

sentences.en: (Photo by Spencer Platt/Getty Images) Turner returns to his fire metaphor.
sentences.zh: （斯宾塞·普拉特/盖蒂图片社拍摄）特纳回到了他的火隐喻。

sentences.en: Fires can have devastating consequences.
sentences.zh: 火灾可能会造成毁灭性的后果。

sentences.en: When the dot-com bubble burst, nearly 5k companies went under and the Nasdaq fell 77%.
sentences.zh: 当互联网泡沫破灭时，近 5000 家公司破产，纳斯达克指数下跌 77%。

sentences.en: The year the housing bubble burst, 860k American properties were repossessed.
sentences.zh: 房地产泡沫破灭那一年，86 万套美国房产被收回。

sentences.en: Still, he says, technology bubbles tend to leave less damage, in part an overvaluation and subsequent crash still leaves behind a real, tangible product we can use.
sentences.zh: 不过，他表示，技术泡沫往往造成的损害较小，部分原因是估值过高和随后的崩盘仍然留下了我们可以使用的真实、有形的产品。

sentences.en: “Fire can be good for some ecosystems,” he says.
sentences.zh: “火灾对某些生态系统有益，”他说。

sentences.en: “Fire revitalizes.
sentences.zh: “火能恢复活力。

sentences.en: That’s true with a lot of technological bubbles, they actually help revitalize the ecosystem.”
sentences.zh: 许多技术泡沫确实如此，它们实际上有助于振兴生态系统。”

sentences.en: Consider the dot-com boom and bust.
sentences.zh: 考虑一下互联网泡沫的繁荣和萧条。

sentences.en: It minted millionaires and led to a recession, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，它创造了百万富翁并导致了经济衰退。

sentences.en: “It also gave us the internet.
sentences.zh: “它还为我们提供了互联网。

sentences.en: We got this amazing information communications technology infrastructure build-out,” he says.
sentences.zh: 我们建立了令人惊叹的信息通信技术基础设施，”他说。

sentences.en: “And, you know, society benefitted from it.”
sentences.zh: “而且，你知道，社会从中受益。”

blocks.html_en: Five experts weigh in.

sentences.en: Five experts weigh in.
sentences.zh: 五位专家发表了看法。

blocks.html_en: The mania had started with something real. The safety bicycle: equal wheels, pneumatic tires, a chain drive. The first bicycle model where the rider’s feet could actually touch the road if they needed to stop.

sentences.en: The mania had started with something real.
sentences.zh: 这种狂热是从一些真实的事情开始的。

sentences.en: The safety bicycle: equal wheels, pneumatic tires, a chain drive.
sentences.zh: 安全自行车：等轮、充气轮胎、链条传动。

sentences.en: The first bicycle model where the rider’s feet could actually touch the road if they needed to stop.
sentences.zh: 第一款自行车模型，如果骑手需要停下来，他们的脚实际上可以接触到路面。

blocks.html_en: Too bad speculators didn’t keep their feet on solid ground.

sentences.en: Too bad speculators didn’t keep their feet on solid ground.
sentences.zh: 可惜投机者没有脚踏实地。

blocks.html_en: “Suddenly, everyone wants to own a bicycle,” says Will Quinn, associate professor of finance at Queen’s University Belfast and co-author of Boom and Bust: A Global History of Financial Bubbles.

sentences.en: “Suddenly, everyone wants to own a bicycle,” says Will Quinn, associate professor of finance at Queen’s University Belfast and co-author of Boom and Bust: A Global History of Financial Bubbles.
sentences.zh: “突然之间，每个人都想拥有一辆自行车，”贝尔法斯特女王大学金融学副教授、《繁荣与萧条：全球金融泡沫史》一书的合著者威尔·奎因 (Will Quinn) 说道。

blocks.html_en: The year was 1897 and the bicycle boom had hit Birmingham hard. Tradesmen north of the city bent and brazed steel into frames. When the owner of Dunlop Tires, Ernest Terah Hooley, saw the surge, he jumped. He bribed journalists, packed company boards with noblemen and bought companies for cheap and sold them to the public at a markup.

sentences.en: The year was 1897 and the bicycle boom had hit Birmingham hard.
sentences.zh: 那是 1897 年，自行车热潮对伯明翰造成了沉重打击。

sentences.en: Tradesmen north of the city bent and brazed steel into frames.
sentences.zh: 城北的商人将钢材弯曲并钎焊成框架。

sentences.en: When the owner of Dunlop Tires, Ernest Terah Hooley, saw the surge, he jumped.
sentences.zh: 当邓禄普轮胎的老板欧内斯特·泰拉·胡利（Ernest Terah Hooley）看到这种激增时，他跳了起来。

sentences.en: He bribed journalists, packed company boards with noblemen and bought companies for cheap and sold them to the public at a markup.
sentences.zh: 他贿赂记者，让贵族挤进公司董事会，低价收购公司，然后加价向公众出售。

blocks.html_en: Ernest Hooley, one of the British entrepreneurs behind the Birmingham bicycle boom. He’d go on to declare bankruptcy four times. (Photo by the Print Collector/Getty Images)

sentences.en: Ernest Hooley, one of the British entrepreneurs behind the Birmingham bicycle boom.
sentences.zh: 欧内斯特·胡利（Ernest Hooley）是伯明翰自行车热潮背后的英国企业家之一。

sentences.en: He’d go on to declare bankruptcy four times.
sentences.zh: 他随后四次宣布破产。

sentences.en: (Photo by the Print Collector/Getty Images)
sentences.zh: （印刷品收藏家/盖蒂图片社拍摄）

blocks.html_en: People began daytrading bicycle shares. Nearly every small bicycle company in Birmingham, ~400, went public; there was a rush on the London Stock Exchange and share prices boomed by 10x.

sentences.en: People began daytrading bicycle shares.
sentences.zh: 人们开始进行自行车共享的日内交易。

sentences.en: Nearly every small bicycle company in Birmingham, ~400, went public; there was a rush on the London Stock Exchange and share prices boomed by 10x.

content_html_zh: 五位专家发表了看法。 这种狂热是从一些真实的事情开始的。 安全自行车：等轮、充气轮胎、链条传动。 第一款自行车模型，如果骑手需要停下来，他们的脚实际上可以接触到路面。 可惜投机者没有脚踏实地。 “突然之间，每个人都想拥有一辆自行车，”贝尔法斯特女王大学金融学副教授、《繁荣与萧条：全球金融泡沫史》一书的合著者威尔·奎因 (Will Quinn) 说道。 那是 1897 年，自行车热潮对伯明翰造成了沉重打击。 城北的商人将钢材弯曲并钎焊成框架。 当邓禄普轮胎的老板欧内斯特·泰拉·胡利（Ernest Terah Hooley）看到这种激增时，他跳了起来。 他贿赂记者，让贵族挤进公司董事会，低价收购公司，然后加价向公众出售。 欧内斯特·胡利（Ernest Hooley）是伯明翰自行车热潮背后的英国企业家之一。 他随后四次宣布破产。 （摄影：Print Collector/Getty Images）人们开始进行自行车共享的日内交易。 伯明翰几乎所有小型自行车公司（大约 400 家）都上市了；伦敦证券交易所一片繁荣，股价飙升了十倍。 研究了 300 年金融泡沫的奎因说：“大约一年后，其中四分之三就破产了。” 当时，《经济学人》写道，投资者认购了数百万美元，“假设价格会维持高位，但这种错觉已被粗暴地击垮了。” 到1898年底，迟到的小投资者损失最大；发起人和早期内部人士早已套现。 但这也不全是坏事：它创造了就业机会。 数千人留下了自行车。 它为后来的汽车工业奠定了基础。 伯明翰的自行车热潮也激发了新的适合自行车的女装设计。 （伦敦立体公司/Hulton Archive/Getty Images 拍摄）从自行车热潮到互联网泡沫，再到今天的人工智能竞赛，金融史上充满了泡沫。 那么当它们弹出时会发生什么呢？ 对于奎因和他的合著者、贝尔法斯特女王大学教授约翰·特纳来说，泡沫是一个糟糕的比喻。 他们更喜欢火。 特纳认为，引发这种火灾的必要因素是： 燃料：低利率和免费信贷。 适销性：监管或技术的变化使人们能够更轻松地买卖泡沫资产。 投机者：新进入市场的投资者，以及无法做空市场的经验丰富的投资者。 特纳说，从那时起，你需要一个火花：一种激进的新技术，比方说，它有望颠覆世界。 需要注意的是，没有人可以预测未来（或者，正如乔治城大学金融学教授 Jim Angel 告诉 The Hustle 的那样，“你真的只能在事后才知道，每个人都在宿醉中醒来，然后问‘我们在想什么？’”），我们请了五位专家来权衡人工智能泡沫对股市、就业市场和美国人的日常生活意味着什么。 对于股票市场 首先，在人工智能上花费的资金是前所未有的。 摩根士丹利 (Morgan Stanley) 预测，到 2028 年，超大规模企业的总支出将达到 1.4 吨。 富国银行估计到 2027 年将达到 1.1 吨。 “这是一笔非凡的资金，”斯坦福经济政策制定研究所幕僚长瑞安·卡明斯 (Ryan Cummings) 表示。 这种支出为 Anthropic、OpenAI 和 Alphabet 等接受支出的公司带来了巨大的收入预期。 “如果你今年没有达到这些收入，明年你就需要更多，”他说。 “随着时间的推移，如果你没有达到这些目标，负担就会增加。” 投资者正在关注人工智能基础设施建设的资本支出与收入的关系。 （摄影：迈克尔·M. 圣地亚哥/盖蒂图片社）并且有充分的理由对 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 即将进行的 IPO 保持警惕。 “所有这些公司都获得了非常非常高的估值，”卡明斯说。 “但它们的定价就好像它们都将成为人工智能的赢家一样。 我们知道并非所有公司都能成功。” 不过，如果泡沫确实破裂，大部分损失将集中在投资者身上，除非主要机构借钱试图利用繁荣。 “直到潮水退去，你都不知道谁在裸泳，”安吉尔说。 “发现一些银行血本无归——这可能会对其他经济领域产生连锁反应。” 对于就业市场 就像其他与人工智能相关的事情一样，专家们对于人工智能对就业市场意味着什么也存在分歧。 “短期内会出现建筑热潮，”科技企业家兼指数观点研究小组创始人阿齐姆·阿扎尔 (Azeem Azhar) 表示。 “从劳动力市场的角度来看，这是一件非常非常好的事情，因为它创造了各种各样的新就业机会。” 阿兹姆·阿扎尔 (Azeem Azhar) 在一场题为“如果这是人工智能泡沫，接下来会发生什么？”的会议上发表讲话 2025 年 11 月。 （摄影：Jordan Peck/Getty Images for Business of Fashion）数据中心基础设施意味着建筑工作——Meta 资助的一份 2025 年报告估计有 470 万个工作岗位。 但这些工作都是暂时的。 数据中心本身只需要 50 到 200 人来运行。 与此同时，根据高盛的数据，过去一年中，人工智能替代每月大约消除 2.5 万个工作岗位，而增强技术则增加了约 9,000 个工作岗位。 “人工智能会因为可以总结电子邮件而抑制办公室工作的理论似乎站得住脚，”他说。 不过，阿扎尔表示，现在判断人工智能将创造什么样的就业机会还为时过早。 他说，当互联网发明时，它催生了现在价值数十亿美元的互补业务。 他预测人工智能将引发同样的创造力激增。 对于你的退休基金如果你是一个年轻人，担心人工智能泡沫对你的退休基金的影响，卡明斯有一条建议。 “看看标准普尔 500 指数的图片就知道了，”他说。 “我只是把钱留在市场上。” 但更广泛地说，泡沫可能引发财富效应。 假设您需要 200 万美元用于退休，而您的 401k 显示您有 250 万美元。 有钱可以花在买一辆漂亮的汽车或装修房屋上。 突然，股市下跌，你的存款看起来只剩下 150 万美元了。 卡明斯说：“你会取消假期，不会得到新车，也不会购买新电器。” “这会导致整个经济下滑。” 卡明斯正在警惕地关注这种可能性。 他表示：“如果 2028 年我们没有出现衰退，我会感到非常惊讶。” 亚马逊在弗吉尼亚州农村地区建立了一个大型数据中心。 （吉姆·韦斯特/UCG/Universal Images Group 通过 Getty Images 拍摄）这可能会让 GenX 面临退休危机。 根据联盟退休收入研究所的一份报告，只有 14% 的人拥有传统养老金，而婴儿潮一代的这一比例为 56%，这使得他们更加依赖股市泡沫的余震。 标准普尔 500 指数花了 500 年才从 2002 年的互联网泡沫破灭中恢复过来：大约用了五年时间才回到高点，然后 2008 年金融危机再次将其摧毁。 直到2013年才完全恢复。 特纳说，这个泡沫的另一个区别是，普通投资者可能没有意识到自己的风险敞口有多少。 在以前的泡沫中，你可以选择是否投资泡沫股票。 如今，约有 23T 美元投资于 ETF，而在互联网繁荣时期，ETF 并没有那么突出。 他表示：“如果你有一只标准普尔 500 指数追踪基金，那么该追踪基金的 35% 都投资于受人工智能热潮推动的七大股票。” “他们将以一种在以前的泡沫中可能没有经历过的方式接触到这种情况。” 对于您的日常生活 泡沫这个词经常被提及。 但潜在的人工智能泡沫与 2008 年的房地产泡沫之间存在着重大区别。 与之前的互联网泡沫一样，迄今为止，人工智能泡沫主要是由股权推动的。 房地产泡沫是由债务支撑的，这使其后果更加深远。 “人们普遍认为泡沫总是很糟糕，”奎因说。 “泡沫的破裂不会对经济造成毁灭性的影响，一点也不。” 无论人工智能是否从根本上改变世界，对于卡明斯来说，解决方案都是一样的。 “它拥有更强大的社会安全网，”他说。 “对于互联网繁荣、金融危机和新冠疫情来说，这都是同样的教训。 您找到失业的人并为他们提供支持。 他们头上有屋顶，肚子里有食物，如果他们有某种健康状况，他们会得到照顾。 人们用很多复杂的方式谈论教训是什么。 事情没那么复杂。” 互联网泡沫破裂后，纳斯达克指数下跌了 77%。 （斯宾塞·普拉特/盖蒂图片社拍摄）特纳回到了他的火隐喻。 火灾可能会造成毁灭性的后果。 当互联网泡沫破灭时，近 5000 家公司破产，纳斯达克指数下跌 77%。 房地产泡沫破灭那一年，86 万套美国房产被收回。 不过，他表示，技术泡沫往往造成的损害较小，部分原因是估值过高和随后的崩盘仍然留下了我们可以使用的真实、有形的产品。 “火灾对某些生态系统有益，”他说。 “火能恢复活力。 许多技术泡沫确实如此，它们实际上有助于振兴生态系统。” 考虑一下互联网泡沫的繁荣和萧条。 他说，它创造了百万富翁并导致了经济衰退。 “它还为我们提供了互联网。 我们建立了令人惊叹的信息通信技术基础设施，”他说。 “而且，你知道，社会从中受益。”
